name: Gwakhyangjeonggi-san (Korean herbal formula; Huoxiang Zhengqi San in Chinese)
short: One 8-week placebo-controlled trial (52 adults with atopic dermatitis, given as granules): no serious adverse events. The abstract gives no data on milder adverse events.
text: A chemical analysis paper gives Gwakhyangjeonggi-san as the Korean name of the formula called Huoxiang-zhengqi-san in Chinese; a Korean case series describes the version its clinic prescribed as made by Lee Je-ma, the founder of Sasang constitutional medicine, and the trial abstract below does not say which version it used. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 52 adults with atopic dermatitis and gastrointestinal symptoms took Gwakhyangjeonggi-san granules (27) or placebo granules (25) for 8 weeks; symptoms fell in both groups without any serious adverse events. The abstract does not report milder adverse events or list the formula's herbs. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
